data: Are the blue squares consistently higher than the red circles?

The question asks whether the blue squares are consistently higher than the red circles in the figure. From the caption, we know that the blue squares represent PKU and the red circles represent MSR. The y-axis represents F1-score percentage, which ranges from 95% to 97%. 

Looking at the data points for each size of beam, the blue squares (PKU) are consistently above the red circles (MSR) across all beam sizes. This is evident because the blue squares are positioned higher on the y-axis compared to the red circles for every value of beam size shown in the figure. Therefore, the blue squares are indeed consistently higher than the red circles.
